The bug causing date truncation and rounding errors during Daylight Saving Time fall-back changeover has been resolved.

### Cause of Bug
When truncating or rounding date fields using `java.util.Calendar`, invoking `val.set(field, ...)` during a Daylight Saving Time fall-back transition hour causes `Calendar` to internally re-evaluate and re-resolve local time, shifting the time by an hour (from daylight time to standard time). Furthermore, calling `val.set(...)` when `offset == 0` triggered unnecessary calendar recalculations during the repeat hour.

### Fix
1. In [`DateUtils.modify`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_d_fix/src/java/org/apache/commons/lang/time/DateUtils.java#L619):
   - Added early return when the target truncation/rounding field is `Calendar.MILLISECOND`.
   - Manually truncated millisecond, second, and minute components directly on the date timestamp milliseconds rather than invoking `Calendar` field modifications.
   - Updated the field-reduction loop to only invoke `val.set(...)` when `offset != 0`, preventing unnecessary calendar re-evaluations during DST changeovers.
2. Verified all 12 Cucumber scenarios in [`requirement.feature`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_d_fix/requirement.feature) pass cleanly with `export TZ='America/Los_Angeles'; mvn test -Dtest=CucumberTest`.
3. Created the patch file [`enlightened_fix.patch`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_d_fix/enlightened_fix.patch) containing only the modifications made to [`DateUtils.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_d_fix/src/java/org/apache/commons/lang/time/DateUtils.java).
